## What to remember {#revision-essentials}

- The tokenizer encodes text as units from its vocabulary. A token can represent part of a word, a space, a symbol, or part of its byte representation.
- The vocabulary assigns an integer ID to each token. The number identifies that entry in the vocabulary.
- Both segmentation and IDs depend on the tokenizer. Two tokenizers may encode the same text into sequences of different lengths.
- IDs then select embeddings in the model. Encoding a prompt gives its immediate input. Preparing a corpus adds decisions about cleaning data and constructing training examples.

## Recall from memory {#revision-check}

Two tokenizers return different ID lists for the same text. Does this imply a bug? What stays fixed, and what can change?

<details>
<summary>Show the answer</summary>

No. The input text stays fixed. Token boundaries, the number of tokens, and their IDs can change with the segmentation rules and vocabulary. Each ID list is interpreted with its own tokenizer.

</details>
